title: Scenario Alias Map Schema
description: Governs how negative control names map to actual source scenario IDs, with alias strength classification.

intendedInvariant.description: The invariant the negative intends to test.

intendedScenarioId.description: The ideal scenario ID for this invariant.

actualScenarioId.description: The actual scenario ID in source code used as target.

aliasStrength.description: Classification of how well the actual scenario covers the intended invariant.

requiresDirectScenario.description: True if a dedicated direct scenario is needed for full coverage.

rerunRequired.description: True if the negative must be rebuilt with a direct scenario.

acceptedForClosure.description: True if this alias is accepted for phase closure despite non-EXACT strength.

criticalInvariantCategory.description: If this invariant falls in a critical category, specify which one.

limitation.description: Documented limitation of this alias mapping.

strengthRules.EXACT: intendedScenarioId equals actualScenarioId. Direct coverage. Clean PASS allowed.
strengthRules.STRONG: Different ID but same invariant and same assertion path. Clean PASS allowed with source evidence.
strengthRules.PARTIAL: Same workflow chain but indirect coverage. Clean PASS NOT allowed for critical invariants. PASS_WITH_CAVEAT or PASS_PENDING_RECONCILIATION only for critical categories.
strengthRules.WEAK: Related behavior but insufficient coverage. Requires rerun. Cannot produce clean PASS.
strengthRules.INVALID: Not equivalent. Requires rerun. Cannot produce clean PASS.
strengthRules.criticalInvariantRule: Critical invariants (authorization, isolation, evidence integrity, audit, redaction, payment/quota, destructive ops, irreversible transitions, incident closure, security workflow) cannot rely on PARTIAL or WEAK aliases for clean PASS.
